subject: Sovereign handshake — acceptance checklist & regional peering questions
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Kim <anna.kim@eurobank.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 05 Nov 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Sovereign handshake — acceptance checklist & regional peering questions

Anna —

Thanks for the quick call yesterday. Per our discussion, I've attached a concise handshake checklist for Redwood Private (VPC) so your legal and cloud teams can sign off on the residency constraints and failover plan. Top-line asks in this note:

- Can your team confirm the exact data-centre CIDR(s) where the private deploy will be allowed (we need IP ranges for allowlist and peering ACLs)?
- Do you require cross-border encryption-at-rest keys to be held in a dedicated HSM in-region? If so, provide KMS/HSM contact.
- For failover ordering between EU and APAC, do you prefer active-active with geo-routing, or active-passive warm-standby? We included both options in the checklist.
- Any additional contractual residency clauses we should mirror in the Playbook (RTO/RPO targets, audit window)?

Attachments: redwood-sovereign-handshake-checklist.xlsx (checklist), eu-apac-peering-draft.png (logical sketch).

Next steps: If you can return the checklist with comments, Laura and I will incorporate and route to our Legal (Aditya) for the final DSA addendum. Happy to hop on a quick tech follow-up with Marco if they want clearer NAT/peering details.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions – Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0191

From: Anna Kim <anna.kim@eurobank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Rojas <m.rojas@sovereign-cloud.com>, legal@sovereign-cloud.com
Date: Sat, 06 Nov 2027 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sovereign handshake — acceptance checklist & regional peering questions

Marcus —

Thanks for sending this through. A few clarifications from our infra team (Marco copied):
1) CIDR ranges: EuroBank will provide a /22 allocation for the EU control plane and a separate /22 for the EU data zone. We need Redwood to support static eBGP peering and RFC1918 ranges — Marco will send exact prefixes by COB Mon 8 Nov.
2) KMS/HSM: We mandate an in-region HSM for key custody. Legal will need the vendor attestation; see attached supply-chain-snapshot.pdf.
3) Failover: We prefer active-passive warm-standby (EU primary, APAC warm) for the first 12 months to simplify control-plane auditing. Can you confirm expected RTO and the test window?
4) Audit: EuroBank requires a 30-day audit log retention window accessible to us; is that compatible with Redwood's Private retention config?

We'll review the checklist and return with inline comments. Marco — please coordinate the network prefixes and any firewall egress expectations.

Best,
Anna Kim
VP, Cloud Architecture
EuroBank
anna.kim@eurobank.com

From: Marco Rojas <m.rojas@sovereign-cloud.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Anna Kim <anna.kim@eurobank.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Nov 2027 08:47:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sovereign handshake — acceptance checklist & regional peering questions

On Mon, 08 Nov 2027 at 08:03 Anna Kim <anna.kim@eurobank.com> wrote:
> Marcus —
>
> Thanks for sending this through. A few clarifications from our infra team (Marco copied):
> 1) CIDR ranges: EuroBank will provide a /22 allocation for the EU control plane and a separate /22 for the EU data zone.

Marcus / Redwood team — attaching the exact prefixes now. Note the EU data zone will terminate behind our perimeter NAT and we expect Redwood to initiate peering from your side to avoid inbound NAT traversal. We also need to confirm TLS mutual auth on the peering session and an agreed MTU (we're at 9000).

Attached: supply-chain-snapshot.pdf (per Anna), and a network sketch in eu-apac-peering-draft.png.

I'll schedule a short call Wednesday to validate BGP session parameters unless you'd prefer email.

Cheers,
Marco Rojas
Sovereign Cloud — Connectivity Lead
m.rojas@sovereign-cloud.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Kim <anna.kim@eurobank.com>, Marco Rojas <m.rojas@sovereign-cloud.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 09:36:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sovereign handshake — acceptance checklist & regional peering questions

Anna / Marco —

Appreciate the prefixes and the HSM confirmation. A few actionable items from Redwood:
- RTO/RPO: For the warm-standby topology we typically target RTO=15 minutes (control-plane failover) and RPO=30s for cached context; we'll provide the runbook excerpt that shows automated HA failover steps.
- Audit logs: Redwood Private can be configured for 90-day or 365-day retention; we will set 30-day retention for the initial deployment and can extend via the retention addendum.
- Peering and NAT: We'll initiate the BGP session from the Redwood side to avoid inbound NAT. TLS mutual auth is supported. MTU 9000 is fine; we'll add jumbo-frame checks to the health probes.

Next steps:
1) Aditya — can you prepare the DSA addendum clause referencing HSM attestation and the audit window?
2) Marcus / Vivek — please prepare a short failover acceptance test plan (30–60 minute window) so EuroBank can schedule a test slot.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Deployments
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Kim <anna.kim@eurobank.com>, Marco Rojas <m.rojas@sovereign-cloud.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 15:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sovereign handshake — acceptance checklist & regional peering questions

Anna —

I've drafted the DSA addendum and included a short paragraph on HSM vendor attestation and audit log retention. Link to the draft in HubSpot (see Related Links). A few legal notes:
- We'll reference the supply-chain-snapshot.pdf as the attestation artifact; Sovereign Cloud should confirm the signing authority on that doc.
- The DSA addendum will include the RTO/RPO targets you accepted above and an audit evidence clause for quarterly checks.

Please review the DocuSign link once Laura and Marcus confirm the final checklist edits. Happy to take any redlines.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Counsel
Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
